description: Spatial post-process/effect-fade correction presets: a live effect whose row references one of these entries tints the battle-area post-process volume while its attack volume reaches the player or camera.

ID.technical: FName row key. AGameEffect::Initialize resolves EffectRow.Id_EffectColorCorrect over EffectColorCorrectDataTables (+0x6A0) and registers the effect with the manager; each tick the battle system re-resolves the same ID and uses Row->Id as the key of Area.ActiveCorrections / ReleasingCorrections. 34 exported rows.

Radius.simple: Horizontal reach of the correction around the effect.
Radius.technical: float cm. For an attack collision sphere the reach is SphereRadius + Radius; for a capsule, Radius is added to the closest-point-on-segment distance (character/capsule radii included); for a plain effect with Height<=0 the reach is mean ActorScale * Radius; with Height>0 the segment reach is (Scale.X+Scale.Y)/2 * Radius. Culling tests use Radius * Culling_ScaleRate. Exported example: 50.0.

Height.simple: Vertical extent of the correction around the effect.
Height.technical: float cm. With bUseAttackCollisionEnabled=false: Height<=0 selects a mean-scale sphere using Radius; Height>0 selects a vertical segment from Location.Z +/- Height*Scale.Z/2, using PointDistToSegment. For capsule attack collisions, Height extends the capsule half-height of the test segment (and ScaleRate*Height for the culling segment). Exported example: 0.0.

bCheckUpperOnly.simple: Reject effects above the character/camera height.
bCheckUpperOnly.technical: bool. When true and bCheckCharacterLocation is true, the row is rejected if either CameraLocation.Z or CharacterLocation.Z is below the effect's Z (i.e. the effect must be above both). Takes precedence over bCheckLowerOnly in the else-if chain. Export example: false.

bCheckLowerOnly.simple: Reject effects below the character/camera height.
bCheckLowerOnly.technical: bool. Checked only when bCheckUpperOnly is false; with bCheckCharacterLocation true it rejects the effect if its Z is below either CameraLocation.Z or CharacterLocation.Z. Export example: false.

bCheckCharacterLocation.simple: Use the player character as a distance test point.
bCheckCharacterLocation.technical: bool. Enables the character location in the upper/lower height gates and in all sphere/capsule/segment distance tests (otherwise only the camera may count). Export example: true.

bCheckCameraLocation.simple: Use the camera as a distance test point.
bCheckCameraLocation.technical: bool. Enables camera location in the height gates and distance tests; for capsules the camera test is only attempted when the character test did not already put the row in range. Export example: true.

Culling_ScaleRate.simple: Outer-radius multiplier that fades the effect instead of applying the correction.
Culling_ScaleRate.technical: float. When != 1.0, a second, larger reach (Radius/Height scaled by this value) sets bInCulling: the effect actor's hidden-in-game flag is set to bCullingEnabled and it fades toward 1 over CrossFadeTime; when ==1.0 the ordinary in-range state is also treated as culling (the row comment says 'within Radius * Culling_ScaleRate: the effect fades out'). Export example: 1.0.

SaturationRate.simple: Saturation multiplier while the correction is active.
SaturationRate.technical: FVector4 (X,Y,Z,W exported). The area tween starts at the post-process volume's BaseSaturation and targets Row.SaturationRate * BaseSaturation over FadeInTime with linear easing; on release it eases from the current value back toward the stored start over FadeOutTime scaled by fade-in progress. Export sample: (1,1,1,1) i.e. no change.

ContrastRate.simple: Contrast multiplier while the correction is active.
ContrastRate.technical: FVector4; same tween pattern as SaturationRate with Area.BaseContrast as the starting value. Export sample: (0.8,0.8,0.8,1.0) for FX_CP_140_09101, i.e. 80% contrast.

GainRate.simple: Gain multiplier while the correction is active.
GainRate.technical: FVector4; same tween pattern with Area.BaseGain as the starting value. Export sample: (0.3,0.3,0.3,1.0).

FadeInTime.simple: Time to blend the correction in.
FadeInTime.technical: float seconds used for all three color tweens and stored in FGameBattleAreaColorCorrect.FadeInTime. On release, the fade-out duration is scaled by GetElapsed()/FadeInTime (or 1 when FadeInTime<=0) so partially faded-in corrections unwind proportionally. Export sample: 0.1.

FadeOutTime.simple: Time to blend the correction out after the effect leaves range.
FadeOutTime.technical: float seconds stored on the correction; used as the duration of the release tweens after the fade-in-progress scaling. A correction stays in ReleasingCorrections until its color/blendable tweens finish. Export sample: 0.1.

ForceCorrectTime.simple: Time window in which the correction is forced without attack collisions.
ForceCorrectTime.technical: float seconds compared with Effect.LifeElapsedTime. While 0 < LifeElapsedTime <= ForceCorrectTime, the attack-collision-enabled check is skipped; after that time, the collision list must contain at least one component with collision enabled, and when bUseAttackCollisionEnabled=false the row is skipped entirely after ForceCorrectTime. Export values are 0.0 in the sampled rows.

DelayCorrectTime.simple: Delay before the correction can apply.
DelayCorrectTime.technical: float seconds; the battle system skips the row while Effect.LifeElapsedTime < DelayCorrectTime (only when the field is >0). Export values are 0.0 in the sampled rows.

bColorCorrectEnabled.simple: Master enable for the post-process colour change.
bColorCorrectEnabled.technical: bool. A row in range is added to RowsInRange only when this is true AND the spawned effect's own bColorCorrectionEnabled flag is set; it does not gate effect hiding/fading or the Niagara parameter. Export sample: true.

bCullingEnabled.simple: Hidden-in-game flag applied to the effect while in the culling band.
bCullingEnabled.technical: bool passed verbatim to IGameActorInterface.SetHiddenInGameFlag when bInCulling is true. Effects are never hidden through this path outside the culling band; CrossFadeTime controls the accompanying fade. Export sample: false.

bUseAttackCollisionEnabled.simple: Whether range is measured against the effect's attack collision shapes.
bUseAttackCollisionEnabled.technical: bool selecting between two range algorithms: true uses the effect's attack collision sphere/capsule components (with Radius/Height expansion); false uses a sphere or vertical segment around the effect actor's location. Also gates the ForceCorrectTime post-window skip. Export sample: false.

NiagaraParameterName.simple: Niagara float parameter toggled 0/1 with in-range state.
NiagaraParameterName.technical: FName; skipped when None. On effect initialization, zero is written to every UNiagaraComponent (0x141320851); each tick the battle system writes 0 when neither in-range nor culling, and 1 when either is true. Export sample: None (unused in these 34 rows).

PostProcessMaterial_Name.simple: Name of a blended post-process material in the area volume.
PostProcessMaterial_Name.technical: FName looked up in Area.BlendableWeights (built from the post-process volume's WeightedBlendables by object name). When found, a FGameBattleAreaBlendableWeight tweens that blendable's weight from its base value to PostProcessMaterial_Weight. Export sample: None (no extra blendable in these rows).

PostProcessMaterial_Weight.simple: Target weight for the named post-process material.
PostProcessMaterial_Weight.technical: float; used as the goal of a linear float tween (exponent 2, 2 args) from the area's base blendable weight over PostProcessMaterial_Time. Only read when PostProcessMaterial_Name resolves in Area.BlendableWeights. Export sample: 0.0.

PostProcessMaterial_Time.simple: Blend time for the post-process material weight tween.
PostProcessMaterial_Time.technical: float seconds passed to the blendable weight interpolator together with PostProcessMaterial_Weight; on release the interpolator is restarted using its current/start values and elapsed time. Export sample: 0.0.

CrossFadeTime.simple: Duration of the effect actor's fade while entering/leaving the culling band.
CrossFadeTime.technical: float seconds passed to AGameEffect::FadeTo(0.0, CrossFadeTime) when not culled and FadeTo(1.0, CrossFadeTime) when culled, only for effects with bFadeEnabled. It is distinct from the post-process colour correction's FadeInTime/FadeOutTime. Export sample: 0.0.

Id_RemoveEffectColorCorrect.simple: Other correction IDs to cancel when this row activates.
Id_RemoveEffectColorCorrect.technical: TArray<FName> (3 slots in every exported row, None padded). When the row is in range, each non-None ID is removed from Area.ReleasingCorrections before this row's own ID is also removed there; the row's own ID then goes into ActiveCorrections. This lets higher-priority effects cancel fading-out corrections. Export sample: three None entries.

notes: EffectColorCorrectDataTables is manager slot +0x6A0; the name is registered at GameDataTableManager.cpp:408 and resolved at line 236. The join is from EffectDataTable.Id_EffectColorCorrect (row +0x150), so a correction row is only evaluated while an effect that names it is alive and registered in GameEffectManager.ColorCorrectEffects.

The range test first honours DelayCorrectTime (effect life) and attack-collision availability, then optional upper/lower height rejection, then either attack collision shapes or an actor-centred sphere/vertical segment, and finally the culling band. Character/camera test points come from AGameCameraManager.GetCameraLocation() and the character actor location.

Area corrections are keyed by row ID in two maps (ActiveCorrections/ReleasingCorrections) on each 'BattleAreaPostProcess'-tagged APostProcessVolume; the tween object layout is decomp-pinned in GameBattleSystems_A.h (0x1D0 bytes).
No localization variants or numbered shards of this table exist in the export; the 34 rows are distinct effect-specific presets.

usages.detail: Effect initialization resolves Id_EffectColorCorrect, zeroes the row's Niagara parameter on all components and registers the effect in ColorCorrectEffects.
Battle system tick (retail 0x100d3e0) evaluates every registered correction effect against character/camera range and builds RowsInRange.
Applies each in-range row to every area post-process volume: color/contrast/gain tweens, optional blendable weight tween and cancellation of removed IDs.
Rows no longer in range are eased back toward base values and moved from ActiveCorrections to ReleasingCorrections until tweens finish.
